purpose: Memory-model research probes and production sparse-VMA validation; sections retain their own code and binary provenance.

metadata.method: Two fresh processes per size/mode, reverse mode order on second pass. 64/256/1024MiB, no guest data accessed; runtime asserts zero guest resident bytes. hardware Registry only: no HVF vCPU. ru_maxrss is process high-water RSS in Darwin bytes, not current live RSS or kernel metadata. Native and PROT_NONE controls do not implement the complete accessible guest mapping semantics.

first_touch.method_note: Native and hardware-only use the same assembly store/stride/branch loop. Hardware-only runs at EL1 with uniform preinstalled 2MiB blocks, no Linux syscalls, VFS, quota/COW/4KiB subrange semantics; evidence is a phase lower bound, not an application speedup. Native pthread and Trames use the same C fixture, 1 thread, 256MiB, 1 recreate round, 1 word per 4KiB with checked values. Original no-metrics Trames runner; ordinary desktop remained, no builds/profilers or other test runners during measurements. Packaged C probes add SPDX/scope comments to measured source, with checked recompiles separately verified.
first_touch.method: five fresh processes per variant, seeded shuffled order, same 256MiB and checked word/page values; hardware-only is EL1 with preinstalled block translations, not a Linux runtime

validation.probes: Rust format, release lint with -D warnings, release build with product overflow-checks; both C sources compile -Wall -Wextra -Werror; native/HVF/fixture checksum controls pass
validation.product: No production source or runtime pin changed. Existing product validation reused; no new Geekbench result or Firefox run.

interpretation.scope: This ratio is headroom in a bounded first-touch phase, not a forecast of total Geekbench/Firefox speedup. Stable-mapping memory stores are already close to native in this loop.
interpretation.priority: Common sparse VMA/resident-extent representation plus a Mac native anonymous backing provider; range publication after that foundation. Keep one userspace Linux kernel shared with iPad.

production_sparse_vmas_2026_10_29.metadata_mode_note: The historical dense CLI mode creates an accessible RW private anonymous mapping; the after implementation represents it sparsely.

evidence.method: Sequential fresh processes in seeded shuffled order. Same Linux static pthread fixture and normal signed no-diagnostics Mac runner. Linux CI VM stopped; no builds/profilers/other tests. Thread timing sums overlap; wall is guest workload duration, not summed thread time.

production_sparse_vmas_2026_10_29.remaining_work: Hardware first touch still uses 4KiB page exports/faults. Native anonymous range backing and block translations remain separate work. The bounded memory medians and the separately completed full Geekbench run have different scopes.

invalidated_prior_geekbench.reason: Multi-core PDF exposed a VMA/retirement cross-product traversal; sampled and deliberately stopped. Replaced by direct store tickets and incremental overlap-index updates. No complete score.

limitations: One clean complete run per final revision; no confidence interval or claim of improvement for every subtest.
Native macOS uses different OS/binary/library/ISA dispatch and reports 24GiB versus the explicit 4GiB guest cap. Ratios are platform results, not isolated HVF cost.
Twelve-slot Text Processing remains below its single-core result; Photo Library and several image components did not improve versus the prior twelve-slot run.
No Firefox recovery or interactive GUI performance claim follows from the CPU benchmark.

provenance_note: Top-level product_source_mac/runtime_revision describe the original research; production_sparse_vmas_2026_10_29 records the implemented path separately.

mechanism: A shared HardwareRange owner retains stable initialized demand-zero bytes and linear GPA/host-VA geometry. The Mac provider lazily registers a private 2MiB allocation; data is not memset or icache-published in bulk.
Uniform RW anonymous extents use L2 blocks, removing per-4KiB HVC/export/Frame creation. Later common CPU/native accesses refer to the same canonical bytes and existing hardware-borrow/region gates.

Append-only insertion-stable range publication lets running interpreter/hardware peers find new private-anonymous RW mappings after a cold lookup miss. No new coordination thread or ordinary memory barrier.
Destructive generations rotate the publication owner. Retained views keep immutable old indexes; shared frame caches are never pruned through the unique-snapshot mutation path.
Precise affected-chunk invalidation, sparse COW population including nonresident contents, pressure eviction and old-VM backing/account transfer retain existing semantics.

shared_mm_acceptance.case: Real interpreter CLONE_VM peer acquires a published pointer and reads 17 from the new mapping in its original running View

bounded_memory_lifecycle.method: Five shuffled fresh processes per variant/cap/workload. Normal signed releases, no diagnostics/metrics/builds/samplers/CI VM, same unmodified static Linux pthread fixture and checksums. auto is host-managed for both; 4096 is the same strict resident cap for both. Thread phase times overlap and are not added to derive wall time.

remaining_limits: Native ranges require default host-managed local and aggregate budgets, uniform RW private-anonymous ownership, no preexisting competing reached-page backing, and no explicit resident working-set target. Other pages retain original per-4KiB exports.

A pure new eligible mmap uses the existing owner/service queue without pausing same-mm peers. Unmap, permission changes, discard, fixed/file/shared mappings, tracing and seccomp retain joined boundaries.

A live fragment/subpage can retain its complete 2MiB host virtual backing. Actual physical residency is host-paged in 16KiB granules; block translations do not require contiguous host physical memory. No claim of 4KiB host reclamation within a retained extent.

Provider residency reports are host-granule counts, not unique physical/PSS accounting. Fork population includes compressed/paged-out data using Mach dispositions; query failure conservatively describes the complete range. Fork/account rebinding can still charge conservatively.

Retained memory after VM destruction falls back to canonical individual pages as old owners rebind. Page accounting follows the new backing and old storage survives only while legitimate owners remain.
Strict 4096MiB microbenchmark controls retain per-page admission; observed median wall changes are +1.54% / -4.27% / +5.48%. No stable strict-cap improvement is claimed.
Memory lifecycle results do not predict Firefox or whole-program speedups. Firefox stayed closed; normal syscall exits and file/shared-page work remain.

excluded_geekbench_diagnostic.reason: Multi-core Photo Library took over 9x the matching baseline stage without completing; sampled for diagnosis. This run is excluded from the clean paired comparison.
excluded_geekbench_diagnostic.cause: Proc refresh repeated mincore-backed residency observations for every task sharing one mm and again for totals. Fixed by one live query per real address-space owner per snapshot, reused for totals and per-thread rows. No cross-request TTL or cached mapping-generation residency.
excluded_geekbench_diagnostic.regression: 13 shared-mm tasks; one provider callback per refresh; the next refresh observes changed residency; zombie owner does not hide live peers.
